e.summary_en: This is a reproducible artefact that uses a machine-readable reporting standard as a verification base in order to score a language model numeric claims, describing itself in writing as a reproducible and traceable pipeline with a standard-grounded oracle for evaluating numeric fidelity. **Measured this round**: published on the ninth of September inside the window, typed as software, licensed under a permissive attribution licence, and shipped as a single archive, accompanying a paper that decomposes numeric fidelity in financial statement analysis into definitional and computational parts and was presented at a workshop co-located with a major natural language processing conference. **This entry belongs to the round theme of targeted gap filling and follows the plan of making standards executable, because the standards category held twenty-six entries in which the protocol-server, skill, and model forms were all empty.** **Four things are worth reading: it turns the question of who computed it correctly into something recomputable, since the pipeline rebuilds intermediate management balances and the ratio cascade from regulatory filing facts to produce a deterministic oracle and then scores each model numeric claim against it, which means the verification base is not another model but a chain re-derived from primary filed facts; the scoring separates three things, namely value fidelity, attribution to the source fact, and error propagation along the ratio dependency graph, which correspond to whether the number is right, whether the citation is right, and whether the derivation is right; it also includes a prompt contrast between pinned and unpinned conditions and an any-standard-definition oracle as a control; and its domain is general corporate finance rather than insurance, which this entry states plainly while noting why the method transfers, since the solvency and reporting standards used in insurance are carried in the same machine-readable format.** **The artefact was neither downloaded nor run this round.**
e.body:
**XBRL-grounded LLM oracle**（Zenodo `10.5281/zenodo.22678122`）**是一份**把**机器可读报送标准**（**XBRL）**当**核验底座**、**给 **LLM 的**数字主张**打分**的**可复现工件****——**逐字自述为**「**A reproducible, traceable pipeline and XBRL-grounded oracle for evaluating LLM numeric fidelity in corporate-finance analysis**」**。**⭐ 本条目属于本轮主题**「**按最薄类目定向补**」**，**并**走**方案 B（**把**标准做成**可执行形态）**。

**可核实信息（均 2026-09-12 Zenodo 记录接口实测）**：

**⭐⭐⭐ ① 它**把**「**谁**算得**对**」**变成**可复算**的**问题****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**记录**逐字**说明**其**管线**由 **SEC EDGAR** 的**事实**重算**「**intermediate-management-balances (SIG)**」**与**「**ratio cascade**」**，**构成**一个**确定性**的 **XBRL-grounded oracle**，**再**对**每个**模型的**数字**主张**打分**；**⭐ 本词条认为**这一处**是**本条**最值得**迁移**的**方法**：**⭐ 即**「**核验**」**不**靠**另一个**模型**，**而**靠**从**原始**事实**重新**推导**的**一条**链**——**⭐ 对 RIAA**：**若**你**要**让 **AI** 处理**任何**结构化**报送**（**偿付能力、**IFRS 17、**年报）**，**则**「**确定性**重算**＋**逐项**比对**」**比**「**再**叫**一个**模型**复核**」**可靠得多**（**⭐ 与**第 373 轮**记下的**「**确定性地基**」**同向）**。

**⭐⭐ ② 三个**评分**维度**被**分开**，**而**这**正**对应**实务**里**三种**不同**的**错误****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**记录**逐字**列出**：**值保真度**（**value fidelity）**、**来源事实**归属**（**source-fact attribution）**与**沿**比率**依赖 **DAG** 的**误差**传播**（**error propagation along the ratio dependency DAG**）**；**⭐ 本词条认为**这一**拆分**对**保险**报送**尤其**贴切**：**⭐ 即**「**数字**对不对**」**、**「**引用**的**来源**对不对**」**与**「**推导**链条**对不对**」**是**三种**可**分别**考核**的**能力**——**⭐ 而**多数**评测**只**看**第一项**，**于是**一个**会**猜**数字**的**模型**与**一个**会**读**报表**的**模型**得**分**相近**。

**⭐⭐ ③ 它**还**做了**两类**对照**，**而**对照**本身**是**方法**的一部分****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**记录**逐字**含 **`A pinned/unpinned prompt contrast`**（**钉住／**不钉住**提示词**的**对照）**与 **`an any-standard-definition oracle`**（**一个**允许**任何**标准定义**的**对照** oracle）**；**⭐ 本词条**认为**这**一点**值得**单独**记**：**⭐ 即**「**核验底座**」**若**不**设**对照**，**就**无法**说明**分数**来自**「**算**对了**」**还是**来自**「**口径**松**」**——**⭐ 对 RIAA**：**做**任何**评测**，**都**应**至少**有**一个**「**更**宽松**的**评判**」**作为**对照**。

**⭐⭐ ④ ⚠️ 域**与**迁移性**必须**同时**说清****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**记录**逐字**说明**其**域**为**「**corporate-finance analysis**」**，**数据**来源**为 **SEC EDGAR**（**一般**企业**报送）**；**⭐ 本词条**如实指出**：**⭐ 即**它**不**是**保险**工具**——**⭐ 而**其**方法**可**迁移**的**理由**是**载体**相同**：**Solvency II** 与 **IFRS 17** 的**报送**同样**以 **XBRL** 表达**，**而**保险**的**比率**级联**（**赔付率、**费用率、**偿付能力）**与**本条**的**财务**比率**级联**在**结构上**同类**；**⭐ 故**本词条**把它**记在**「**数据与标准**」**而**不**是**「**精算专业工具**」**，**并**在**此**标注**它是**跨域**方法**样本**。

**⭐⭐ ⑤ 发布形态**与**可引用性****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**记录**类型逐字为 **`software`****、**发布日 **`2026-09-09`****（**窗口内**）**、**许可逐字 **`cc-by-4.0`****、**文件**逐字**为 **`finrun-paper-0.3.0.zip`****、**DOI **`10.5281/zenodo.22678122`****；**⭐ 记录**并逐字**说明**它是**论文**「**Definitional or Computational? Decomposing LLM Numeric Fidelity in Financial-Statement Analysis with an XBRL Cascade Oracle**」**的**软件**与**冻结结果**工件**（**作者 **Oussama Chahed**，**FinNLP 2026**，**EMNLP 2026** 同期**），**⭐ 即**「**论文**＋**冻结结果**」**一起**发布**——**⭐ 对 RIAA**：**这**是**一种**值得**照抄**的**作品**交付**方式**（**⭐ 与**本站**已收的**日本医保**复现**归档同形）**。

**⭐⭐ ⑥ 与池内条目的关系**：**本站 [[brel-xbrl]] 是**XBRL** 解析**库**、**[[morphir]] 覆盖**以 **DSL** 表达**金融**逻辑**、**[[edgartools]] 覆盖**美国**证券**报送**数据**、**[[ifrs17-calculation-engine]] 覆盖**新准则**计算**——**⭐ 而**本条补上的是**「**把**报送**标准**当**核验**底座**、**并**按**三个**维度**给**模型**数字**主张**打分**」这一**形态**；**⭐ 本词条**不对以上任何一条做代码级比较**。

**对 RIAA**：**⭐ 五件事值得借**：**① **核验**用**确定性**重算**，**而**不**是**再**叫**一个**模型**；**② **把**「**值**对、**引用**对、**推导**对**」**分开**打分**；**③ **评测**要**有**更**宽松的**对照**；**④ **跨域**方法**要**写清**域**与**迁移**理由**；**⑤ **论文**工件**要**冻结**结果**并**给 **DOI**。

**⚠️ 本词条如实标注**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次**没有下载**其工件、**没有运行**其管线**（**未**取回 **`finrun-paper-0.3.0.zip`**、**未**复现**任何**评分**）**，**故**不主张**其**评分**结果**、**也**不主张**其 **oracle** 的**正确性**。**② ⚠️ 本次**只读**Zenodo 记录接口返回的**元数据**（**标题、**描述、**类型、**许可、**文件**名与 **DOI）**，**未读**其**论文**正文**、**未读**其**代码**。**③ ⚠️ **未核实**其**论文**是否**已**通过**同行**评审**（**⭐ 记录**逐字**只**说明**为 **poster**）。**④ ⚠️ **未核实**其**得分**差异**是否**来自**方法**而**不**来自**提示词**选择**（**⭐ 本词条**只**记录**其**含**对照**）。**⑤ ⚠️ **未核实**其**方法**在**保险**报送**（**Solvency II／**IFRS 17）**上**是否**已**有人**实施**——**⭐ 本条**的**迁移**说法**是**本词条**的**判断**，**而**不**是**其**工件**的**主张**。**⑥ ⚠️ 本条目**所记为 **2026-09-12 所见**；**⚠️ 该工件**是**研究方法**材料**，**不是**审计**意见**，**也**不是**合规结论**。

**XBRL-grounded LLM oracle**（Zenodo `10.5281/zenodo.22678122`）**是一份**把**機器可讀報送標準**（**XBRL）**當**核驗底座**、**給 LLM 的**數字主張**打分的**可復現工件****——**逐字自述為**「**A reproducible, traceable pipeline and XBRL-grounded oracle for evaluating LLM numeric fidelity in corporate-finance analysis**」**。**⭐ 本條目屬於本輪主題**「**按最薄類目定向補**」**，**並走**方案 B（**把標準做成可執行形態）**。

**可核實資訊（均 2026-09-12 Zenodo 記錄介面實測）**：

**⭐⭐⭐ ① 把「**誰算得對**」變成可複算的問題****——**記錄逐字說明其管線由 SEC EDGAR 事實重算 intermediate-management-balances (SIG) 與 ratio cascade**，**構成確定性的 XBRL-grounded oracle**，**再對每個模型的數字主張打分**；**⭐ 即**核驗**不靠另一個模型**，**而靠從原始事實重新推導的一條鏈**——**⭐ 與第 373 輪「**確定性地基**」同向**。

**⭐⭐ ② 三個評分維度分開****——**逐字為**value fidelity**、**source-fact attribution**、**error propagation along the ratio dependency DAG**；**⭐ 即**「**數字對不對**」「**引用對不對**」「**推導對不對**」**是**三種**可分別考核的能力**。

**⭐⭐ ③ 兩類對照****——**逐字含** A pinned/unpinned prompt contrast** 與 **an any-standard-definition oracle**；**⭐ 即**核驗底座若無對照**，**就無法區分「**算對了**」與「**口徑鬆**」**。

**⭐⭐ ④ ⚠️ 域與遷移性****——**逐字為 corporate-finance analysis**，**數據來自 SEC EDGAR**；**⭐ 即**它不是保險工具**，**而**方法可遷移的理由是載體相同**（**Solvency II 與 IFRS 17 同樣以 XBRL 表達）**。

**⭐⭐ ⑤ 發布形態****——**類型逐字 `software`**、**發布日 `2026-09-09`（**窗口內**）**、**許可逐字 `cc-by-4.0`**、**文件 `finrun-paper-0.3.0.zip`**、**DOI `10.5281/zenodo.22678122`**；**論文逐字為**Definitional or Computational? Decomposing LLM Numeric Fidelity in Financial-Statement Analysis with an XBRL Cascade Oracle**（**FinNLP 2026、**EMNLP 2026 同期）**。

**⭐⭐ ⑥ 與池內條目的關係**：[[brel-xbrl]]、[[morphir]]、[[edgartools]]、[[ifrs17-calculation-engine]]——**⭐ 本條補上的是**「**把報送標準當核驗底座、**並按三維度打分**」**這一形態**。

**對 RIAA**：**⭐ 五件事值得借**：**① **用確定性重算核驗**；**② **三維度分開打分**；**③ **評測要有更寬鬆的對照**；**④ **跨域方法寫清域與遷移理由**；**⑤ **論文工件凍結結果並給 DOI**。

**⚠️ 本詞條如實標註**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次**沒有下載**其工件、**沒有運行**其管線**，**不主張**其評分結果與 oracle 正確性**。**② ⚠️ 本次**只讀 Zenodo 記錄介面的元資料**，**未讀**其論文正文與代碼**。**③ ⚠️ **未核實**其論文是否已通過同行評審**（**逐字只說明為 poster**）**。**④ ⚠️ **未核實**其得分差異是否來自方法而非提示詞選擇**。**⑤ ⚠️ **未核實**其方法在保險報送上是否已有人實施**——**遷移說法是本詞條的判斷**，**不是**其工件的主張**。**⑥ ⚠️ 本條目所記為 2026-09-12 所見**；**⚠️ 該工件是研究方法材料**，**不是**審計意見**，**也**不是**合規結論**。
e.body_en:
This is a reproducible artefact that uses a machine-readable reporting standard as a verification base in order to score a language model numeric claims. **This entry belongs to the round theme of targeted gap filling, and it follows the plan of making standards executable.**

**Verified information, all measured on 2026-09-12 from the record interface**:

**First, it turns the question of who computed it correctly into something recomputable.** The record states that the pipeline rebuilds intermediate management balances and the ratio cascade from regulatory filing facts into a deterministic standard-grounded oracle, and then scores each model numeric claim against it. **Verification here does not rest on a second model but on a chain re-derived from primary facts, and for any structured filing such as a solvency return, an insurance contract reporting package, or an annual report, deterministic recomputation with item-by-item comparison is far more reliable than asking another model to check.**

**Second, the scoring separates three things that correspond to three different failures.** The record lists value fidelity, attribution to the source fact, and error propagation along the ratio dependency graph. **In reporting work, whether the number is right, whether the cited source is right, and whether the derivation chain is right are three separately assessable capabilities, and most evaluations look only at the first, so a model that guesses numbers and a model that reads statements can score alike.**

**Third, two controls are built in, and the controls are part of the method.** The record names a prompt contrast between pinned and unpinned conditions and an any-standard-definition oracle. **Without a looser comparison the verification base cannot distinguish a score that comes from computing correctly from one that comes from a permissive definition, so any evaluation should carry at least one more permissive judgement as a control.**

**Fourth, the domain and the transferability have to be stated together.** The record describes the domain as corporate-finance analysis with data drawn from regulatory filings of listed companies. **This is not an insurance tool, and the reason the method transfers is that the carrier is the same, since the solvency and accounting standards used in insurance are expressed in the same machine-readable format, and the ratio cascades involved, such as loss ratio, expense ratio, and solvency coverage, are structurally the same kind of thing as the financial ratio cascade used here, which is why this entry files it under data and standards rather than under actuarial tooling and marks it as a cross-domain method sample.**

**Fifth, the release form supports citability.** The record is typed as software, published on the ninth of September inside the window, licensed under a permissive attribution licence, shipped as a single archive, and carries a persistent identifier, and it explicitly describes itself as the software and frozen-result artefact for a paper presented at a financial technology workshop co-located with a major conference. **Releasing a paper together with frozen results is a delivery pattern worth copying, and it matches the form of a reproducibility archive already on the site.**

**Sixth, relative to existing entries**: pooled entries cover a reporting-format parsing library, a domain-specific language for financial logic, a filing data toolkit, and an accounting-standard calculation engine, **while this entry supplies the form in which a reporting standard becomes the verification base for scoring model claims across three dimensions. This entry makes no code-level comparison against any of them.**

**For RIAA**: **five practices transfer: verify by deterministic recomputation rather than with another model; score value, citation, and derivation separately; keep a looser judgement as a control; state the domain and the reason a method transfers; and freeze results behind a persistent identifier when releasing research.**

**Marked honestly by this entry**: **first, the artefact was neither downloaded nor run**, no archive was retrieved and no score was reproduced, **so no claim is made about its results or the correctness of its oracle**. **Second, only the metadata returned by the record interface was read**, not the paper text or the code. **Third, whether the paper has passed peer review was not verified**, the record describing it only as a poster. **Fourth, whether the score differences come from the method rather than from prompt choices was not verified**, and this entry records only that controls are present. **Fifth, whether the method has been applied to insurance reporting by anyone was not verified**, so the transferability claim is this entry judgement rather than the artefact own claim. **Sixth, this entry records what was visible on 2026-09-12 and states plainly that the artefact is research method material rather than an audit opinion or a compliance conclusion.**
